title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Hazard Classes, Packing Groups and Contract Rating by Category
content:
Dangerous Goods Acceptance is offered in six categories, ranked 1 to 6. For each of them this card fixes which IMDG classes or divisions are taken, which packing groups are taken, whether the goods have to travel packed as IMDG limited quantities, and whether the booking carrying them has to be rated under a service contract.

| Rank | Category | IMDG classes or divisions taken | Packing groups taken | Must be packed as limited quantities | Booking must be contract-rated |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | AHL DG Limited Quantity | 2.2, 3, 4.1, 5.1, 6.1, 8, 9 | II, III | Yes | No |
| 2 | AHL DG Class 9 Standard | 9 | II, III, none | No | No |
| 3 | AHL DG Flammables and Corrosives | 3, 4.1, 8 | I, II, III | No | No |
| 4 | AHL DG Toxics and Oxidizers | 5.1, 5.2, 6.1 | I, II, III | No | No |
| 5 | AHL DG Compressed Gases | 2.1, 2.2, 2.3 | none | No | Yes |
| 6 | AHL DG Special Approval | 1.4S, 4.2, 4.3, 7 | I, II, III, none | No | Yes |

In the packing-group column, the entry none stands for goods declared without any packing group.

## Reading the card

- A class or division that is listed in no row has no category at all in this product.
- Several classes are listed twice: 2.2, 3, 4.1, 5.1, 6.1, 8 and 9 each appear under rank 1 and again under a higher rank. Of the two rows, only rank 1 carries the limited-quantity packing obligation.
- Packing group I is taken only by ranks 3, 4 and 6.

## Points of judgement

**Does a No in the last column forbid a contract-rated booking?** It does not. The column records whether contract rating is demanded; a No means that no such demand is made for that category.

**What does Yes in the limited-quantity column mean in practice?** Goods admitted under AHL DG Limited Quantity are goods packed as IMDG limited quantities; that packing is part of what the category is.
